title: Navigation landmark
body: Which element should wrap a site's main navigation links?
explanation: Semantic elements (`<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>`, `<article>`, `<footer>`) create landmarks that screen-reader users can jump between.

title: alt text for decorative images
body: How should a purely decorative image be marked up?

options.e: Missing alt makes screen readers announce the file name.

explanation: Informative images need concise alt text describing their purpose; decorative ones use alt="" (or CSS backgrounds) so assistive tech skips them.

title: button vs clickable div
body: Why prefer `<button>` over `<div onclick>` for actions?

options.t: Buttons are focusable, keyboard-operable (Enter/Space) and expose the button role to assistive technology by default

answer: Native semantics and keyboard support for free.
explanation: A div needs role="button", tabindex="0" and key handlers to approximate it. Remember buttons inside forms default to type="submit".

title: Associating labels
body: How do you associate a `<label>` with an `<input id="email">`?

options.t: Place the label after the input

answer: Use the for attribute (or wrap the input in the label).
explanation: Clicking the label focuses the input and screen readers announce the label. Placeholders are not a substitute for labels.

title: input type=email

options.t: Built-in format validation and an email-optimised keyboard on mobile devices

answer: Client-side validation and better mobile keyboards.
explanation: Client-side validation is a UX feature only; always validate on the server too.

title: defer vs async scripts
body: How does `<script defer>` differ from `<script async>`?

options.t: defer scripts execute in document order after parsing completes; async scripts execute as soon as they download, in any order
defer only works for inline scripts

answer: defer = ordered, after parsing; async = ASAP, unordered.
explanation: Both download in parallel without blocking parsing. Use defer for app code with dependencies and async for independent scripts like analytics. Module scripts are deferred by default.

title: First rule of ARIA
body: What is the 'first rule' of ARIA use?

options.t: Add role attributes to every element
Use a native HTML element with the required semantics and behaviour instead of repurposing an element with ARIA whenever possible
ARIA replaces the need for labels

answer: Prefer native HTML; ARIA only adds semantics, not behaviour.
explanation: Incorrect ARIA is worse than none. Test with a screen reader and keyboard-only navigation.
